items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I suppose that's true. I find it even today that he's one clarinet player you can't speak ill of... And Fozola is one of the gods.

ctx.x: Well, Fozola certainly was highly respected when he was in Chicago working with the Bobcats. And every clarinet player, when they listened on the air, listened for Fozola's solos. I think...

I suppose that's true. I find it even today that he's one clarinet player you can't speak ill of. And there's a bunch of musicians still around Chicago, some of them have emigrated, who collected around Detroit in the late 40s. And they were all keen and hipped on the Bobcats. That was their musical genesis. All the Bobcats. And Fozola was along with them. And Fozola is one of the gods. And there you have it.
Were there other clarinet players with the Bobcats who might have left an influence here, Detroit, or anywhere?
